1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with ample letter spacing, line height, and white space around all text elements across every screen.

2.why: No italics or all-caps appear in instructions; text is short sentences or labels without dense paragraphs.

3.why: Layouts are single-column cards with large touch targets and generous padding that remain readable and uncluttered at mobile widths.

4.why: All instructions are one or two plain-language sentences (e.g., “Enter the six-digit identity code”).

5.why: Some fields show format hints (placeholder “6 digits”, recovery-code example ABCD-1234-EF56-7890) but many inputs lack any example of expected content.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than a brief sentence or a short list of codes before the primary action is available.

7.why: The long authenticator secret and recovery codes are rendered as ordinary selectable text in the page, so they can be copied, although no explicit copy button is provided.

8.why: The setup screen mentions “scanning a code” yet never displays a QR code or any other scannable alternative; only the raw secret string is shown.

9.why: Standard HTML inputs are used, so browser autofill could work for email/phone, but there is no evidence of autocomplete attributes, one-time-code support, or password-manager integration for secrets or OTPs.

10.why: Page titles clearly name the current step and the primary action is always a prominent full-width blue button.

11.why: Most screens present a single primary button; the authenticator-provisioning and regenerate screens temporarily show multiple fields but still emphasize one confirm action.

12.why: Success messages such as “Authenticator verification succeeded” and “Recovery code accepted and permanently consumed” appear, though they do not always explicitly state the next step.

13.why: “Start over”, retry after errors, and “Regenerate recovery codes” are always available with no lock-out or penalty indicated.

14.why: The only error shown (“The request could not be completed.”) neither explains the problem (invalid code) nor tells the user how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown timers, session timeouts, or other time limits are visible on any screen for reading or code entry.
